summary: Phase-3 Disaster Recovery endpoints + UI verified. Backend: 8/8 pytest cases PASS in /app/backend/tests/test_recovery.py. /api/bootstrap/status -> {fresh:false, user_count>0}. /api/admin/backups/verify with test_plain.zip -> 200 {valid:true, encrypted:false, total_documents:3, has_code:true, has_env:true}. /api/admin/backups/verify with test_encrypted.zip + 'TestPass1234567890' -> 200 {valid:true, encrypted:true, total_documents:3}. Missing-passphrase -> 400 with 'encrypted/passphrase required'. Wrong-passphrase -> 400 'Could not decrypt backup — wrong passphrase.'. /api/admin/backups/test-sandbox with encrypted ZIP + correct pass -> 200 with restored counts + comparison object; production /api/stats counts (total_tools, total_dealers) UNCHANGED before & after, and top-level stats keys identical (prod untouched). 401 enforced on /api/admin/backups/verify and /api/admin/backups/test-sandbox when called without bearer token. Frontend: logged-in admin loads /admin/backups successfully. 'Disaster Recovery' section renders with dr-full-snapshot, dr-verify, dr-sandbox PillButtons all present. 'Restore from Google Drive' lists 12 .zip rows each with testID starting 'dr-restore-' (real Drive file ids visible, e.g. dr-restore-1dUGWFpo8JVv_10gLKO2MhxTGDOpXdnps). Tapping a row opens the confirmation Modal with dr-confirm-email TextInput + dr-confirm-restore PillButton + Cancel button (verified by screenshot). Auth-routing regression check: clearing localStorage and visiting root lands on /login (NOT /bootstrap) — DB-not-empty rule honored. NO destructive endpoints were invoked. NOTE: The per-row 'Restore' TouchableOpacity on the Drive list is visually clipped on a 390-px wide screen (its bounding box is only 30 px wide on the right edge, and the label text 'Restore' is cut to 'Restor'); the button still works but is hard to tap with a finger.

ui_bugs.component: admin/backups.tsx — Restore from Google Drive row 'Restore' button
ui_bugs.issue: On 390-px wide mobile viewport each dr-restore-{id} TouchableOpacity bounding box is only ~30 px wide (x=328, width=30) and the visible label is clipped to 'Restor'. Cause: in styles.driveRow the right-side action button uses flex:0 with paddingHorizontal:14 but the parent row gives the LEFT name+date View flex:1 with no maxWidth, so when filename is long the action gets squeezed off-screen. Playwright click via mouse only opened the modal when bypassed via dispatchEvent; real touch in some areas would miss.

design_issues.screen: admin/backups.tsx — Restore from Google Drive list
issues: Long filenames (e.g. '06-05-2026 11-45 FULL SNAPSHOT.zip') push the right-aligned Restore button partially off-screen on a 390 px viewport.
Suggestion: set the name View to flex:1 with minWidth:0 (or use numberOfLines + flexShrink) AND give the Restore button a fixed width / minWidth so it stays fully visible & tappable.
Existing console deprecation warnings persist: 'textShadow*' style props (use textShadow), props.pointerEvents (use style.pointerEvents). Cosmetic only — non-blocking.

action_items: Fix the clipped Restore button on the Drive list in /app/frontend/app/admin/backups.tsx — wrap the filename column with minWidth:0 (or flexShrink:1) and give the action button a fixed width like 96–110 px so the label stays visible on 390-px screens.
(Optional) Add testID='dr-confirm-cancel' to the modal's Cancel TouchableOpacity for future automated cancel-flow tests (currently only a textual 'Cancel' control).
critical_code_review_comments: recovery.py is a well-isolated module: a single asyncio.Lock prevents concurrent restores, every production restore takes a pre-restore safety snapshot via backups._create_backup_doc, and every action writes a restore_log entry — solid auditability.
_parse_backup_bytes correctly distinguishes ZIP vs gzip vs plain-JSON and surfaces a CLEAN 400 'Could not decrypt backup — wrong passphrase.' when pyzipper raises on bad keys (verified live).
_sandbox_db uses real_db.client[real_db.name + '_sandbox'] and is dropped immediately after the test_sandbox endpoint completes — confirmed prod stats unchanged in pytest.
AES-256 (WZ_AES, nbits=256) via pyzipper for full_snapshot; passphrase NEVER embedded in archive — only mirrored to Drive as 'X PASSPHRASE.txt'. Matches the user's Phase-3 spec.
Bootstrap endpoint correctly returns 410 if user_count>0 (closes the public restore window) — verified indirectly by /api/bootstrap/status returning {fresh:false, user_count>0}.
Restore-from-drive auto-fetches the companion passphrase file when caller omits it AND the ZIP is encrypted — nice UX safeguard.
Frontend _layout.tsx auth routing no longer regresses: unauthenticated root navigation lands on /login (NOT /bootstrap) because DB is non-empty.
Minor: admin/backups.tsx is now ~890 lines (over the 700-line guideline) — splitting Disaster-Recovery UI into its own component (e.g. <DisasterRecoveryPanel/>) would help.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% — all required testIDs present and modal opens with correct controls; one clipped-button UX issue on Drive rows.

seed_data_creation: No new seed data created. test-sandbox uses a throwaway sibling DB that is auto-dropped after the call (verified — no _sandbox DB lingers).

rca_of_issue: The clipped Restore button (frontend issue) is layout-only — in admin/backups.tsx driveRow the name column is flex:1 but lacks minWidth:0, so on narrow screens with long filenames the Restore TouchableOpacity (flex:0, paddingHorizontal:14) gets pushed past the right edge of the parent container; only ~30 px remains hit-tappable and only 'Restor' renders. Fix: add {minWidth:0} (and ideally numberOfLines wrapper) to the name View AND set a fixed minWidth on the action button.
